executiveSummary: GM1955's official 2025 identity, contained centre, 36,996 residents, 27 neighbourhoods, twelve BAG places, twenty settlement labels, Didam railway station and ten Dutch NWB border links are internally coherent; neighbourhood population differs by only 21 residents (-0.057%) and is reconciled without rewriting source observations. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Montferland spans two materially different systems: the elevated, wooded Bergherbos/stuwwal, and the low Liemers river-clay landscape protected by Rhine/IJssel dikes and connected across the German border. The municipal adopted climate plan says every core contains roads and buildings that flood in its 70 mm/hour stress test, emergency routes can become impassable, most cores are vulnerable in a dike-breach model, and the Bergherbos ridge and parts of adjacent cores remain dry. The canonical river case instead produces exactly 3.059067 of legacy depth-like amplitude and up to 18,774 affected resident-equivalents without choosing dike section 48-1/48-2/48-3, a Dutch or German breach, footprint, arrival or recession; its exact local ranking does not resolve the dry ridge. Pluvial allocation is similarly generic. A controlled ignition at the Bergherbos-area neighbourhood centre ranks its source neighbourhood only twenty-fourth of 27, while unrelated hazards reuse the same leading neighbourhood order. The transport graph stops at Dutch municipal boundaries and omits Germany, the A12-A3 continuation, cross-border bus 91, Emmerich acute care and event-valid border/closure state. Exact service and recovery values omit the documented drainage assets, physical utility topology, acute-care routing, nature-fire operations and accountable first-72-hour actions. Public observations and registers remain context only; Unknown and NoData must never be presented as zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1955 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK/BRT source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1955 as Montferland in Gelderland and reports 36,996 residents, density 350/km2, 25.1% aged 65 or older and 5,072 one-person households. The generated centre [6.21141941094202, 51.9063299545864] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Twenty-seven neighbourhood rows in three districts sum to 36,975 residents, 21 below the municipality total (-0.057%); households sum to 16,360 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 9,295. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 36,996 without altering source values.

BAG supplies twelve current woonplaatsen and BRT supplies twenty settlement labels: twelve woonkernen, six buurtschappen and two gehuchten. All place reference points are contained in the generalized boundary; labels remain neither occupancy nor service/catchment footprints.

Most statistic fields cover all 27 neighbourhoods, but home value, cars per household, benefit/pension/social-security, tenure and housing fields each have at least one NoData row; district heating and public charging cover 0/27. Null, suppression, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Adopted climate-adaptation plan, municipal water-system inventory and local impact mechanisms
evidenceSources.edition: Klimaatadaptatieplan Montferland adopted at the end of 2021; current climate/water pages and 2026 budget/GWRP inventory inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality's 70 mm/hour stress test finds roads and buildings with water nuisance in every core and explains that sewer pipes cannot carry such an extreme shower. Streets and public-space flow routes are part of the solution; the statement is an official scenario finding, not a current flood observation.

The adopted plan says most cores are vulnerable in a dike-breach model, while only the Bergherbos on the push moraine and parts of surrounding cores stay dry. It warns that roads used by emergency services can become impassable. The plan does not publish an incident-time breach, probability, depth or route status.

The plan identifies drying of Bergherbos/heath and associated nature-fire risk, plus heat impacts on older residents, roads, rail and installations. These are planning mechanisms rather than current ignition, fuel moisture, exposure, damage or service state.

The municipal 2026 inventory describes approximately 136 km mixed sewer, 107 km foul sewer, 34 km storm sewer, 38 km infiltration sewer, 140 km pressure sewer, 39 system pumps, 611 pressure units, two tunnel pumps, one groundwater pump, twenty wadis and three retention basins. Design inventory is not connectivity, current operation, spare capacity, backup or restoration. No standard machine reuse licence or event cadence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027 and Liemers cross-border flood-system description
evidenceSources.edition: Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027, officially published 30 November 2021; Liemers/Veluwe area story inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Rijn en IJssel distinguishes the high Montferland and Veluwe infiltration ridges from the flat Liemers river-clay landscape containing old Rhine branches and no single clear main watercourse. This terrain and system split is not represented by administrative-centroid proximity.

The Liemers is largely enclosed by primary Rhine/IJssel dike systems; the programme identifies dike sections 48-1, 48-2 and 48-3. A selected flood simulation therefore requires a named defence state and connected hydraulic footprint.

The authority states that a dike breach on the German side can inundate Dutch territory and that Dutch and German partners cooperate on high-water actions. A graph clipped to Dutch municipality adjacency cannot represent this source or response dependency.

The programme and area story establish long-lived mechanisms and governance, not current river level, dike condition, breach, inundation, pump/weir setting, groundwater or T+72 recovery. Official-publication reuse applies to the published programme; linked map content retains its own metadata.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 and Dutch-German crisis-cooperation programme
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 appendices published March 2025; current ERMWIC page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The regional profile reports 1,811 hectares of nature in Montferland and assesses nature-fire scenarios including forest crown/ground fire and heath fire. Area is exposure context, not fuel continuity, ignition probability, current fire perimeter or suppression state.

The region's adopted risk set includes flooding, extreme weather, heat/drought, nature fire, utilities, cyber/telecom and transport disruptions. A regional hazard family does not validate a municipality-specific amplitude or service curve.

The current ERMWIC programme states that disasters do not stop at the border and improves fire, rescue, ambulance and crisis cooperation among VNOG/Gelderland and German Kreis Kleve/Düsseldorf partners through exercises running to 2027.

Plans and cooperation arrangements establish roles and possible mutual aid, not event-time alerting, availability, border passage, requested resources, arrival, task completion or restoration. No blanket standard redistribution licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — A12/A3, rail, transit and event-valid German-border access context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal notice published 31 August 2026, valid 4 September 20:00 through 7 September 2026 05:00; NWB-Light 1 August 2026 and ProRail/GTFS snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The municipality announces a planned A3 closure between the Beek border and Emmerich-Oost and a detour via A18, N316 and the Emmerich ring, warning that local roads may be busier. The future-valid restriction is dated operational evidence for a calendar-bound exercise only, not a timeless scenario default.

A municipal 10 March 2026 notice says German border controls cause regular A12 queues, accidents and diversions over local roads affecting Beek and Elten. It establishes a recurring cross-border access mechanism, not present speed or capacity.

The municipality identifies Didam on the Arnhem–Winterswijk railway and cross-border bus 91 between 's-Heerenberg and Emmerich. The deployed context contains Didam station and 37 GTFS stops, but schedules/points do not establish event operation, passengers, accessibility, capacity or recovery.

The monthly CC0 NWB logical graph has ten Dutch cross-boundary links over A12, A18, N316, N335, N812, N813, N815 and N816 toward Zevenaar, Doetinchem and Oude IJsselstreek. It has no German municipality/road continuation; consecutive same-corridor sections are series, not additive emergency capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM / Slingeland Ziekenhuis / PRO HOMINE St. Willibrord-Spital Emmerich
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Domestic register coverage and cross-border acute-care dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026, CC0; hospital public pages current/updated 3 January 2025 and inspected 3 September 2026
supports: RIVM assigns no acute-care department inside GM1955. Nearest straight-line reference-point records are Slingeland Doetinchem 9.311 km, Rijnstate Arnhem 23.195 km, Gelre Zutphen 24.083 km and Radboudumc 25.757 km; registered roles and distance are not travel time, acceptance, staffing, beds or capacity.

Slingeland states that its emergency department in Doetinchem is open 24/7 and has a dedicated ambulance entrance. That is service-role information, not live occupancy, diversion, power/oxygen, supplies or route state.

The official St. Willibrord-Spital Emmerich page describes a 24/7 hospital with 271 beds and a certified local trauma centre. It is outside the national RIVM register and absent from the deployed network; public role information does not establish cross-border dispatch/acceptance or current capacity.

Cross-border and Dutch acute-care journeys require destination-aware ambulance dispatch, passable routes, border arrangements and mutual aid. No public source reviewed supplies incident-time patient demand, acceptance, generator endurance or T+72 throughput.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RWS Waterinfo / KNMI / NDW
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, grid planning, communications, education and bounded observation context
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation contains 58 GM1955 points: ten sewer pumps, two surface-water pumps and 46 weirs. Capacity is present for all sewer pumps but absent for both surface pumps and all weirs; connectivity, compatible units, settings, current operation, reserve, backup and restoration remain unavailable.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Liander service area OS ZEVENAAR10-1i and reports planning capacity, requests, queues and projects with earliest dates from 2030. One at-least-quarterly/monthly planning sample, with exact dataset licence unidentified, is not municipality coverage, live load, outage, switching, reserve or topology.

RDI returns 69 antenna installations, including 31 mobile, sixteen fixed-link, two broadcast and nineteen amateur records; DUO returns eighteen education-location records. Registers do not establish communications coverage/backhaul/power or shelter designation, occupants, accessibility, supplies and live operation. RDI reuse licence/cadence is unstated; DUO is daily CC Attribution, version unspecified.

No RWS Waterinfo observation/forecast or KNMI weather station is assigned inside GM1955. The nearest reviewed Waterinfo point is Lobith/Bovenrijn at 9.795 km with timestamped level/flow and only T+1/6/12/24 forecast horizons; nearest KNMI station is Deelen at 28.717 km. NDW situations nearest the reference point are external and timestamped. No in-boundary match remains NoData, never normal water/weather or open routes.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Current drought/low-Rhine context and Montferland landscape character
evidenceSources.edition: RWS Droogtemonitor issued 18 August 2026; Province Gelderland Liemers landscape guide inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The 18 August 2026 national drought monitor reports historically low Rhine discharge, an average precipitation deficit of about 300 mm comparable with 2018 and groundwater at its lowest level in five to ten years, with effects on navigation, agriculture and nature. It is dated national/regional context, not a local future fire or water-supply trajectory.

The Province's Liemers guide describes the Montferland push moraine with steep slopes and old forest, alongside the A12/A18 corridors. Landscape guidance supplies durable terrain/nature context, not event fuels, moisture, access, traffic or damage.
The dated drought context can inform an explicitly calendar-bound exercise and evidence review, but it cannot silently drive the canonical unbound wildfire, river, drinking-water or recovery curves.

Observation/forecast/landscape evidence retains publisher, issue/observation/valid time, coverage and uncertainty. Missing local measurements or forecasts are Unknown, never evidence of normal conditions.

corrections.summary: Standardize evidence class, time, licence, coverage and NoData semantics across municipality layers and exports.
corrections.validation: Static context, timestamped observation, issued forecast, future-valid restriction, official scenario, manual action and synthetic result are visibly distinct. No in-boundary record and unavailable/null values display Unknown/NoData, not zero, safe, open, available or restored; synthetic flood amplitude is never labelled measured metres.

residualLimitations: No expert-selected WRIJ/RWS/WMCN/LIWO scenario supplies Rhine boundary level/datum, dike 48-1/48-2/48-3 condition, Dutch/German breach/overtopping, connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival, duration, recession and dewatering for GM1955.

The municipal 70 mm/hour stress-test conclusion is authoritative scenario evidence, but the reviewed deployment lacks its licensed cell/road/building footprint, rainfall duration, surface-flow, sewer state, uncertainty and update metadata.
The CBS Verspreide huizen Montferland polygon is broader than the Bergherbos ridge; neighbourhood rank or population cannot prove which ridge/valley cells are wet, burning, reachable or occupied.

The 58 HWH points and municipal design inventory lack complete catchment connectivity, flow direction, compatible capacity units, settings, receiving levels, present condition, backup and restoration; surface water, sewer and drinking water must remain separate.

No public source establishes a current Bergherbos ignition/perimeter, combustible-fuel condition, local wind/plume, visitors, access, extinguishing water, crews or suppression state. The 18 August drought monitor is dated national/regional context.

Ten NWB border links use nominal scenario units and omit Germany, A12-A3 continuation, border-control state, bus 91, rail operation, local detours, cross-border responders and destination-specific emergency throughput.

The officially planned 4–7 September 2026 A3 restriction is future-valid relative to audit time and must not be applied to an unbound exercise; subsequent change/cancellation and exact lane/direction state require refreshed evidence.

No RIVM acute department lies inside GM1955. Straight-line proximity and public roles for Slingeland and St. Willibrord do not establish ambulance time, border passage, acceptance/diversion, staff, beds, power/oxygen, generator fuel or T+72 throughput.
One Liander planning sample and 69 RDI sites do not establish municipality electricity/gas/telecom topology, coverage, live load, outage, backhaul, backup, reserve, switching or restoration.

CBS residents exclude workers, pupils, patients, tourists, cross-border travellers, responders and displaced people; no privacy-safe event-time presence, care-demand or assistance-needs layer is integrated.

No in-boundary Waterinfo, KNMI weather or NDW match is a bounded coverage result. External points and missing records remain NoData, never normal conditions, open access or safety; Lobith forecasts reviewed stop at T+24, not T+48/T+72.

Exact hazard, affected-population, eight-service, recovery and person-hour results remain synthetic exercise outputs, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties or operator commitments until critical/high findings are corrected and reviewed by local and cross-border authorities.
This audit covers the first 72 hours only; flood recovery, nature restoration, repairs, displacement, health effects and cross-border economic disruption can last substantially longer.
provinceReviewFlags: Gelderland, Montferland, Rijn en IJssel, RWS/WMCN, VNOG and German water/crisis partners should define selectable Liemers river/dike/breach, pluvial/drainage and dewatering cases with explicit boundary, defence/control, high-ground cells, footprint, timing, uncertainty and NoData.

Province, municipality, VNOG/Brandweer, nature managers and German partners should review Bergherbos/local nature-fire versus external-smoke cases, valid-time drought/readiness, people presence, access, extinguishing water, warning/closure and suppression state.

Province, RWS, road authorities, ProRail/operators, OV authorities and German partners should review A12-A3, A18/N316 detours, local border roads, Didam rail, bus 91 and route-valid restriction semantics without treating schedule/graph presence as operation.

Ambulance services, Slingeland, St. Willibrord/Emmerich, VNOG and German crisis partners should define privacy-safe cross-border dispatch, acceptance/diversion, route alternatives and mutual-aid state; national-register absence is not hospital absence.

Montferland, WRIJ, utilities and safety partners should review aggregate surface-water/sewer/drinking-water and power/gas/telecom dependencies, backups and restoration while keeping sensitive topology protected and public-register NoData explicit.

Gelderland and cross-border partners should implement one first-72-hour action/resource/evidence contract for warning, water control, evacuation/shelter, access/border, nature fire, care, utilities and resupply, with Unknown/NoData never collapsed to zero or safe.
